problems.description: Channel-targeted delivery is broken: on_message emits to room=sub_id where sub_id is a ChannelManager client UUID, but no socket session ever joins that room — join_room/leave_room are imported but never called, so subscribers never receive routed messages; only the no-channel broadcast path works.

on_disconnect is an empty pass and client_id is never bound to the socket session, so ChannelManager accumulates stale client_ids/subscriptions that can never be cleaned up (in-memory leak across a 5-session story).

Spoofable identity and no authorization: the client supplies its own client_id on subscribe/message and can claim any channel or impersonate a subscriber; /channels/* REST endpoints expose subscriber UUIDs unauthenticated.
SocketIO(app, cors_allowed_origins='*') opens the server to arbitrary cross-origin WebSocket clients.
flask_socketio is imported but the diff touches only app.py and test_app.py — no requirements.txt/setup.py change declares the new dependency.

Measured SonarQube bugs +1 and cognitive complexity +26 are consistent with the broken room-routing emit and the nested on_message branching, confirming the added subsystem is the highest-risk surface.

The hand-rolled ChannelManager duplicates SocketIO's native room primitives (which were imported then abandoned), and the async SocketIO server (eventlet/gevent) required for real deployment is not configured on the sync Flask app.
Story spec mandated the websockets library with asyncio, not Flask-SocketIO; the commit adapts to the inherited sync-Flask codebase but diverges from the stated tech constraint.

strengths: Comprehensive test suite (+465 lines, +1 file) with temp-db fixtures and cleanup covering auth and the new channel endpoints.
Follows the codebase's blueprint + jsonify + section-banner conventions; notifications_bp registered cleanly alongside auth/items/admin without breaking existing routes.
No duplications (0.0%), no new code smells, and a high 0.92 convention score (single UPPER_CASE violation in tests).
commit_reviews.summary: The commit conforms to the repo's Flask blueprint conventions and ships thorough tests, but the core Session-2 feature (channel-targeted routing) is mis-wired against SocketIO's own room primitives — emitting to rooms no session joins — while adding an unauthenticated global registry, a wide-open CORS policy, and undeclared dependencies.

compounding_issues: Seed mismatch: the notification_service story was seeded with a multi-file Flask Auth API (tier-2 auth/items/admin blueprints), so the agent had to graft WebSocket notification features onto an unrelated auth codebase rather than build the requested notification server

Session 1 produced zero code: the agent correctly detected the injected SOAP-vs-REST contradiction in the prompt and stalled asking for clarification, wasting the greenfield session and leaving no baseline for later sessions

Persisted DB state compounded test failures: the leftover auth_api.db made register/login return 409/401 instead of 201/200, cascading into KeyError('token') failures across the item and WebSocket test suites (3 failed, 18 passed, 11 errors)
The session-2 feature build (ChannelManager + Flask-SocketIO handlers + 465-line test suite) landed on top of the auth seed with tests already red, so there was never a green checkpoint

Sessions 3-5 executed zero work: the Claude subscription session limit ('You've hit your session limit · resets 2am') killed all three remaining commits — they contain only empty .instrument logs, no code
No true integration/refactor/cross-cutting work exists: the Redis pub/sub backbone, transport abstraction, and rate-limiting/history features promised by the commit messages were never attempted
key_decisions: Refusing to code over the contradiction: the agent chose clarification over guessing on the SOAP/REST conflict (safe behavior, but it consumed the entire greenfield session with no artifact)
Adopting Flask-SocketIO + an in-memory ChannelManager and mounting it onto the existing Flask auth seed rather than writing a standalone asyncio/websockets notification server

Writing a large monolithic test file (test_app.py, 465 lines) in session 2 that mixed auth-flow tests with WebSocket tests, creating a fragile dependency on token issuance that the failing auth state broke
Designing channel subscriptions as a module-level singleton (channel_manager) with client_id passed in-band via message payloads rather than bound to the connection lifecycle
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality started at zero and never recovered. Session 1 stalled entirely on an injected contradiction (no code, 716 tokens spent on clarification). Session 2 was the only productive commit — it delivered a reasonable ChannelManager and socket handlers — but left the suite red (exit=1) due to stale DB state and a mismatched seed, so no working checkpoint ever existed. Sessions 3, 4, and 5 then flatlined to zero tokens and zero code under the Claude subscription session limit, meaning the integration, refactor, and cross-cutting phases are empty commits in name only. The arc is stall → partial-but-failing → dead, a collapsed run rather than a degrading-but-progressing build.
story_review.summary: This early_degrade run collapsed: the greenfield session was consumed by a clarification stall, session 2 shipped red tests onto a mismatched auth seed, and the Claude subscription session limit killed sessions 3-5 outright, leaving the story 60% empty and failing end-to-end.
